en: Identify direct objects after transitive verbs, apply the masculine accusative shift (der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen), and leave feminine, neuter, and plural articles unchanged.
Estimated time 50 Minutes · Prerequisites: Units 01–07 (Unit 06 conjugation + Unit 07 V2 order)

examples.en: What would you like to drink?
What do you like to eat?

title.en: The Accusative Case (Akkusativ) — Direct Object Shift

notes.en: The Accusative case marks the direct object receiving the action of a verb (haben, trinken, essen, bestellen, kaufen). CRITICAL: ONLY MASCULINE ARTICLES SHIFT IN ACCUSATIVE! Feminine, Neuter, and Plural remain identical to Nominative.
notes.ne: अक्कुसेटिभ केसले क्रियाको (haben, trinken, essen, bestellen, kaufen) कार्य प्राप्त गर्ने प्रत्यक्ष वस्तुलाई चिन्हित गर्छ। महत्त्वपूर्ण: मात्र पुरुषलिङ्गका (masculine) articles मात्र accusative मा परिवर्तित हुन्छन्! स्त्रीलिङ्ग, नपुंसकलिङ्ग, र बहुवचन nominative जस्तैैै हुन्छन्।
notes.de: Der Akkusativ markiert das direkte Objekt, das die Aktion eines Verbs empfängt (haben, trinken, essen, bestellen, kaufen). KRITISCH: NUR MÄNNLICHE ARTIKEL VERÄNDERN SICH IM AKKUSATIV! Feminin, Neutrum und Plural bleiben identisch mit dem Nominativ.

title.en: Accusative Triggers — Verbs Always Taking Direct Objects

notes.en: These verbs ALWAYS require an accusative direct object: bestellen (to order), trinken (to drink), essen (to eat), haben (to have), kaufen (to buy), brauchen (to need), sehen (to see), möchten (would like).
notes.ne: यी क्रियाहरूले सदैँ अक्कुसेटिभ प्रत्यक्ष वस्तु अपेक्षा गर्छन्: bestellen, trinken, essen, haben, kaufen, brauchen, sehen, möchten।
notes.de: Diese Verben ERFORDERN IMMER ein akkusativisches Direktobjekt: bestellen, trinken, essen, haben, kaufen, brauchen, sehen, möchten.

bullets: Ich habe EINEN Kaffee. (Masculine: der Kaffee → einen)
Ich esse EIN Brot. (Neuter: das Brot → ein — unchanged)
Ich bestelle EINE Suppe. (Feminine: die Suppe → eine — unchanged)

payload.explanation: Only masculine articles shift in the accusative: der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen. Feminine, neuter, and plural stay identical to the nominative.

note.en: Trap 1: Forgetting the masculine accusative shift

traps.wrong: Falsch: "Ich schreibe ein Brief." / "Er hat kein Hund."
traps.right: Richtig: "Ich schreibe EINEN Brief." / "Er hat KEINEN Hund."

note.en: Trap 2: Shifting feminine and neuter articles that must NOT change
note.ne: स्त्रीलिङ्ग र नपुंसकलिङ्गका article लाई बदल्नु जुन बदलिनु हुँदैन
note.de: Feminine und neutrale Artikel verschieben, die UNVERÄNDERT bleiben müssen

traps.wrong: Falsch: "Ich esse einen Apfel… nein: Ich esse ein Brot." (das Brot is neuter — stays 'ein')
traps.right: Richtig: "Ich esse EIN Brot." / "Ich trinke EINE Milch." (Neuter and feminine NEVER shift.)

note.en: Trap 3: Using an accusative article on the SUBJECT. The subject stays in the nominative — only the direct object shifts.
note.ne: फन्दा: कर्तामा अक्कुसेटिभ article प्रयोग गर्नु। कर्ता Nominative मै रहन्छ — प्रत्यक्ष वस्तु मात्र परिवर्तित हुन्छ।
note.de: Falle: Einen Akkusativartikel auf das SUBJEKT anwenden. Das Subjekt bleibt im Nominativ — nur das Direktobjekt wechselt.

traps.right: Richtig: "DER Kaffee ist lecker." (Subject = nominative; object = accusative.)

body: 🚨 CRITICAL RULE: In German, only masculine articles change in the accusative. This is a common source of errors even for advanced speakers, because the temptation to 'regularise' die → den, das → das, or eine → eine feels symmetrical but is wrong.

Why it happens: The masculine is the only gender whose article differs between nominative and accusative, so a learner who shifts everything by pattern-matching looks consistent but is wrong three times out of four.
XP Reward: 100 XP | Badge Unlocked: 🎯 Accusative Shift Specialist
